verdictRule: CONSENT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX.
verdictBasis: I found neither a MUST-FIX nor a SHOULD-FIX. Eleven refutation attacks were run against the draft's load-bearing claims and all eleven failed. Every digest the draft asserts was recomputed from disk and matches: the frozen Stage A subject, both Stage A reviews, both frozen turn-1 Stage B reviews, and all four fixture copies. Both Stage A reviews measure ACCEPT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, so the dual-independent-ACCEPT 0/0 predicate holds. The single turn-1 finding, CLAUDE-D302-S-1, is landed in the exact terms its requiredRemedy demanded -- the literal series form 'authored under D-293 Decision 8' attached to the per-D-002-platform copies, carrying the adoption-commit pin -- and the warrant itself verifies independently: D-293 Decision 8 enumerates G21 in the delegated set and commit c10319d207cb90e2bf9df4c5e5997cfd35a30193 resolves to D-293's adoption. Nothing else moved: the frozen artifact, both Stage A reviews and all four copies are unmoved. Every identifier the draft names resolves to a real object with exactly the member list asserted, no identifier is invented, and the draft correctly declines to claim both reviewers' identifiers are preserved, Codex having returned none at either stage. The register effects reproduce: 5 of 32, 28 of 28, DR-G21 OPEN, COORD and file 08 byte-identical to their pins. The three advisories are provenance and wording matters for a successor, none contradicted by any byte I could resolve; they are honesty work, not bars.
